STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Greater one-horned rhinoceros
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The rhino is the living emblem of Assam's wild grasslands.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: The Indian rhinoceros is inseparably tied to Kaziranga National Park, which shelters the majority of the world's wild population. A symbol of strength and survival, it draws visitors from across the globe to the floodplains of the Brahmaputra. Classified Vulnerable by the IUCN, it is both Assam's pride and a global conservation responsibility.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: White-winged wood duck
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: A rare forest waterfowl of Assam's evergreen wetlands.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: The white-winged duck — or deohah — is a large, secretive duck of Assam's tropical evergreen forests and slow rivers, seen at Nameri and the foothill wetlands. Dark-bodied with a striking whitish head, it is among the most endangered waterfowl in the world, listed Critically Endangered by the IUCN and protected under CITES Appendix I.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Foxtail orchid (Kopou phul)
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The bloom that heralds Rongali Bihu across the state.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: The Kopou phul, with its fragrant, densely packed purple-white inflorescences, is woven into the hair of Bihu dancers each spring. Symbolising love, joy and renewal, it is the floral emblem of Assam — its appearance marks the arrival of the Assamese new year.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Hollong
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The royal hardwood of Assam's evergreen forests.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: Hollong is a towering tropical hardwood, 20–30 metres tall, that dominates Assam's evergreen and semi-evergreen forests. Valued for its durable timber, it is sacred to the Moran community and stands as a symbol of the state's forest wealth and ecological heritage.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Kaji Nemu (Assam lemon)
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The GI-tagged lemon declared the state fruit in 2024.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: Kaji Nemu is a slender, seedless variety of lemon indigenous to Assam. Declared the state fruit by cabinet decision on 12 February 2024, it is a Geographical Indication (GI) tagged treasure — used in the famous Khar, in the aromatic 'Masor Tenga', and served to guests after every Assamese meal.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Bihu
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The three-fold festival of Assam's agricultural year.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: Bihu is celebrated three times a year — Rongali (Bohag) Bihu in April, Kongali (Kati) Bihu in October, and Bhogali (Magh) Bihu in January — marking the sowing, growing and harvest of the rice. With the dhol, pepa and gogona, and the woven gamosa, it is the heartbeat of Assamese life.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Bihu Dance
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The state dance, performed at Rongali Bihu.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: The Bihu dance, performed to the rhythm of the dhol and the bamboo clatter of the gogona, is the official state dance of Assam. Danced in circling groups with brisk steps and swaying hips, it is the joyful expression of the Assamese new year — women in muga mekhela-sador, men in dhoti and gamosa.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: O Mur Apunar Dekh
STATE_SYMBOLS.official: অ' মোৰ আপোনাৰ দেশ — 'O My Endearing Country'
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The beloved state anthem of Assam.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: Written by Lakshminath Bezbaroa — the great Assamese poet and novelist — 'O Mur Apunar Dekh' is Assam's official state song. Sung at the start of every official function and assembly, its opening words are a love-letter to the land: 'O my endearing country, the land of red hills and blue rivers.'

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Joi Aai Axom
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The invocation to Assam personified as a mother goddess.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: 'Joi Aai Axom' — Hail Mother Assam — is the officially accredited motto of the state. It invokes Assam as a mother goddess, a land of nurture and pride, and is the resounding greeting of Assamese identity and belonging.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Assamese
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The easternmost Indo-Aryan language, written in its own script.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: Assamese (Axomiya) is the official language of Assam and the easternmost of the Indo-Aryan languages, written in the Assamese–Bengali abugida. Carried by the poetry of Sankardev, the Borgeets and the literature of the Assam Sahitya Sabha, it is the voice of a distinct civilisational identity in the Northeast.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Emblem of Assam
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The official seal carried on the state's correspondence.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: The state seal of Assam is carried on the official correspondence of the Government of Assam and listed on the state's portal as the 'State Seal'. Assam does not have an officially recognised flag; instead a banner displaying the state seal on a plain field represents the Government of Assam.
